sub_agendas_items.title: Duty to Consult - Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act, 2005
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
The following staff provided a slide presentation and answered questions from the Committee:
Committee members asked staff about the criteria involved in upgrading parks with better accessible features.  Members provided staff with feedback on multi-use pathways (MUP) and the difficulties in sharing with bicycles and the lack of space for wider wheelchairs to safely maneuver on pathways.
Staff discussed that as of September 2021, the City has completed protected design guidelines which are used for all new and renewal projects.
The use of delineators and ‘twizzies’ are used to try and separate pedestrians and cyclists. The implementation of these devices is not always possible but the City is trying to make paths wider. The City is introducing delineators in Environmental Assessments (EA) studies in places where there will be cyclists and pedestrians.
Staff are to provide the Committee with literature that is available for educating cyclists to use a bell as they approach pedestrians.
After discussion, the Committee RECEIVED this item for information.
A copy of the slide presentation is filed with the Office of the City Clerk.
